title: Trajectory-Guided Steering: Mitigating Spurious Feature Bias in Clinical Classification
abstract: arXiv:2610.22618v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models rely on spurious features in clinical classification: swapping a single gender token in clinical notes alters gender-irrelevant diagnoses in up to 53.5% of cases. Existing inference-time corrections either need counterfactual data built around the specific spurious feature or behave unpredictably. We observe that how a model's preference between answers evolves across layers, its prediction trajectory, indicates for each document whether a correction is likely to help. We propose Trajectory-Guided Steering (TGS), which decides from the trajectory alone whether to correct each prediction and in which direction, with no counterfactual data and no knowledge of the spurious feature. On 16 clinical classification tasks from i2b2, TGS fixes 17.7% of errors while breaking only 1.3% of correct predictions and stays net-positive across all tested hyperparameter settings; all baselines are net-negative or near zero. translated_title: 轨迹引导转向：缓解临床分类中的伪特征偏差
translated_abstract: 大语言模型在临床分类中依赖伪特征：在临床记录中替换单个性别词元，会使多达53.5%的与性别无关的诊断结果发生改变。现有的推理时修正方法要么需要围绕特定伪特征构建的反事实数据，要么行为不可预测。我们观察到，模型对答案的偏好在各层之间的演化方式（即其预测轨迹）能够针对每个文档指示修正是否可能有所帮助。我们提出了轨迹引导转向（TGS），它仅凭轨迹即可决定是否修正每个预测以及修正的方向，无需反事实数据，也无需了解伪特征。在来自i2b2的16个临床分类任务上，TGS修复了17.7%的错误，同时仅破坏了1.3%的正确预测，并在所有测试的超参数设置下均保持净正向收益；而所有基线方法的净收益均为负或接近于零。
tldr: 提出轨迹引导转向（TGS）方法，仅凭模型内部预测轨迹即可判断是否修正预测及修正方向，无需反事实数据或伪特征知识，在16个临床分类任务上修复了17.7%的错误且仅破坏1.3%的正确预测，并在所有超参数设置下保持净正向收益。
en_tdlr: Trajectory-Guided Steering (TGS) uses only the model's prediction trajectory to decide whether and in which direction to correct each prediction, requiring no counterfactual data or knowledge of spurious features, fixing 17.7% of errors while breaking only 1.3% of correct predictions across 16 clinical classification tasks.
